newsitem.title: ITALY: Committal hearing set for Italy's Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Committal hearing set for Italy's Prodi.

text.p: A hearing to decide whether Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi should stand trial for alleged irregularities while head of industrial holding IRI has been set for January 15, judicial sources said on Thursday.
Prodi has denied allegations of conflict of interest and abuse of office relating to the state-run holding company's sale of a food company, Cirio, to a consortium called Fis.Vi
A deputy public prosecutor in Rome, Giuseppa Geremia, has asked for Prodi and the five other members of the then IRI board to stand trial, alleging IRI granted the buyer an "unjust advantage".
The conflict of interest allegation against Prodi stems from a consultancy he held with Anglo-Dutch group Unilever, which bought part of Cirio from Fis.Vi soon after the IRI sale.

Prodi told state television on Tuesday he was not considering resigning if sent to trial. "It's a hypothesis that I am not raising because there is no element that could suggest going to trial," he said.
